notes.title: ROUGH JUSTICE: '84 MAJOR UPDATE
notes.content:
Greetings Agents!

We're excited to let you know that we have rolled out a MAJOR UPDATE. This update addresses several issues that have been brought to our attention by the helpful community! 

These issues run the gamut from tweaks, to bug fixes and degrinding. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37531502/0e3f743404b5278b57ecd774e93dfec7132e5535.png[/img]

[h2][b]AGENT COSTS[/b][/h2]
Have you ever wanted to hire an agent and you just thought that their rate was a bit too pricey? Fear no more! The Agency Union has been busted, and agent rates have been reduced by 25% across the board. 

[h2][b]AGENT LEVELLING [/b][/h2]
[i]"Ugh, 327 more Security cases until  I can unlock Agent Wheeler to level 10?!" [/i] [b]shakes fist furiously at devs[/b] Well, that sentiment and those like it are a thing of the past. No more endless hours of grinding to level up your agents.

[h2][b]CONTRACT REWARDS[/b][/h2]
We've generously increased the payout of all contracts and tiers across the board, because...you're worth it. 

[h2][b]CASE OFFICER LEVELS[/b][/h2]
We've decreased the case officer reputation required to level up all of the case officers. No more snide remarks from disappointed case officers who disappointedly shake their heads.

[h2][b]ITEMS[/b][/h2]
The cost of items has been reduced by 25%. If you've been eying the Tier 4 Thumper 187 Shotgun, with prices like these, why not pick up two?

[h2][b]UPDATES[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] Achievement icons updated
[/list]
[h2][b]BUG FIXES[/b][/h2]
[list]
[*] LQA fixes for achievements,  puzzle data, tutorial hints, and general text.
[*] Operation lead activation fixed
[/list]
[h2][b]REASONING & JUSTIFICATION[/b][/h2]
Do we [i]REALLY[/i] need to write this? It took us a while to come around, but at the end of the day we want you, the players to HAVE FUN. It was a bit of a wake-up call when we realized that although a lot of players had sunk endless hours into the game, only a small percentage of players actually finished it.  The grindy aspect seems to have prevented players from delving deeper into the story and experiencing the intricate plot twists we've lovingly created. 


We hope that you enjoy this update! 


[h1][b]OUT NOW[/b][/h1]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1291860/Rough_Justice_84/

[h1][b]JOIN OUR DISCORD[/b][/h1] 
Have some feedback? What to chat with the devs and other players? Join our [url=https://discord.gg/roughjustice]discord[/url]. You can join the conversation and hang out with other fans on the discord server and talk directly to us regarding your thoughts and ideas about Rough Justice: '84.

[h1][b]YOUTUBE SHORTS[/b][/h1] 
We've had hundreds of streamers check out the game so far, check out some of the Youtube Shorts from their gamplay experiences on the official[url=https://www.youtube.com/@roughjustice84/shorts] Rough Justice: '84 Youtube Channel[/url].

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37531502/ac30188d7d08259b0dd9f9e96a82d992a2305911.png[/img]

So, it's been a few days since we released, and you guys have been amazing with pointing out the bugs you've found. For those of you that find any more bugs, feel free to hit us up on our discord and post them in the[url=https://discord.com/channels/662375859537313793/1009895260102594570] bug reports channel[/url].  Alternatively, you can use the in-game bug logging feature in the main menu. 

There will inevitably be growing pains, but we're trying to tackle these issues as quickly as we can, ensuring that your playing experience is optimized. So, without further ado, here is the list of bug fixes, balancing and quality-of-life elements that have been addressed in the 1.04 patch.

notes.title: Agent Loyalty
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37531502/14d80e3ae555e5e000048730da83149733ac4ce6.png[/img]


Each agent has a base loyalty value. This is a flexible number that changes depending on the outcome of contracts. If an agent's loyalty dips below a certain level it will have negative implications. On the flip side, if your agent's loyalty is high, then buffs will be activated.

This would be for example a trigger to notify the player that the agent is unhappy. If the agent's loyalty gets to ZERO then another trigger is called, and the agent leaves for good. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37531502/c856f9be4848ae8da84d5dbd53acb76edc700781.jpg[/img]

There are five different loyalty levels.

Level 1:  Agent Wages Increased by 20%   / Travel Costs increased
Level 2:  Agent Wages Increased by 10%  / Travel Costs increased 
Level 3:  No variable changes (baseline)
Level 4: Agent wages decreased by 10% / Travel Costs decreased
Level 5: Agent wages decreased by 20% / Travel Costs decreased

Each agent starts out at level 3, which is the baseline, which does not have any positive or negative implications.

We soft-launched our Alpha Demo about a week ago and we've had plenty of time to gather input.
The number one gripe that a lot of players had was the lack of proper onboarding, which we've now addressed.

After our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1291860/view/3370394584487252658]initial hotfix[/url] to squash a number of nasty bugs we focused on dissecting the general feedback from players and streamers. Thanks to the good folks over at [url=https://gameround.co/detail/263/review/reviews]G.Round[/url] we've been making massive headway, and their input has been invaluable. So, a big shout out to all of the awesome folks over there!


[h2][b]ONBOARDING[/b][/h2]

This is a mechanic that we had been planning on implementing at a later date, but due to the feedback received, we prioritized it. Immersion is everything, and coming to grips with a brand new game with different mechanics can sometimes be a daunting experience. 

Watching streamers become frustrated because they weren't sure about the correlation of certain mechanics was as equally as frustrating for us! We wanted to make the onboarding as enjoyable and straightforward as possible, and we hope we've achieved this. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37531502/6f6a56e3ca95398721f31979426dff6d3d5f02bd.gif[/img]

[h2][b]PUZZLE DIFFICULTY SETTINGS[/b][/h2]

Probably the second most requested feature was the ability to select different difficulty levels with the puzzles.  As previously mentioned, there are 3 different Tiers of difficulty for cases: 

[b]Tier 1 = Easy
Tier 2 = Normal
Tier 3 = Hard[/b]

This is not only reflected in the number of successful rolls required during a case, but also in the puzzles.  This change however only concerns the training center, If you'll remember, the purpose of the training center is to give players an opportunity to try out all of the puzzles and prepare themselves for their usage within cases. Having the ability to choose the difficulty level is essential in this process, as puzzles scale according to case tier difficulty!

Even with the initial addition of the 3 tiers of puzzle difficulty, we realized that it is a lost opportunity not to add a "Tier 0" and a "Tier 4". With these additions we are able to slowly introduce puzzles to new players [Tier 0] and of course challenge the most hardcore members of the community [Tier 4].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37531502/eebee952cab127c673530b896c0c3adc2f467f46.gif[/img]

notes.content:
A lot has changed over the course of the last few weeks, and we here at Gamma Minus would like to show a bit of our progress and the iterations Rough Justice: ‘84 has gone through. Check out the video below to get an overview.

[previewyoutube=h9ywdwtwl4A;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2][b]INFORMATION SECTION[/b][/h2]
Now that a lot of the core mechanics are in the game we realized that it was kind of important to let players know how it’s all interconnected. With our new informative tutorial system, players can scroll through each section and read more about them in detail. This information is readily available at any time when on the main map by clicking on the i button. 
The information provided is not extremely verbose, but if you’re ever stumped as to how something works, or the reasoning behind a particular mechanic, it helps to give the information section a gander.

[h2][b]DIALOGUE SYSTEM[/b][/h2]
The first Operation Lead utilizing our dialogue system is now implemented. It’s still not 100%, but it’s getting there. This is essentially how all of the story elements will be displayed. These are branching dialogs with choices to make as well as challenges to overcome. 

[h2][b]CASE OFFICERS[/b][/h2]
Previously known as “informants”, case officers provide you with bundles of cases, which are referred to as caseloads.  Each case officer offers a specific type of case.

The caseloads are only available for a certain amount of time. If they are not accepted, then they expire and you’ll have to wait until they offer a new caseload. We are experimenting with reputation loss when not accepting caseloads. Some team members think that would be too punishing, but again, it could be a great incentive for all those completionists out there

[h2][b]CASELOAD OVERVIEW[/b][/h2]
When caseloads are completed, reputation with the individual Case Officer is either gained or lost.

[h2][b]CASELOAD REWARDS[/b][/h2]
As previously mentioned, reputation is defined for each individual case officer. The more caseloads that are completed for a particular case officer, the more potential reputation there is to gain. This individual case officer's reputation is directly correlated to their specific reward set.
Action Points in regards to Distance
One of the biggest mechanics that we’ve added is how distance determines the total amount of action points required to send an agent to a location. 

Previously, regardless of the distance, it always cost 1 action point, now, depending on the proximity, it can take between 1 and 3 action points. 

This may seem like a minor detail, but it really requires you to plan out your cases accordingly, and even plot out a planned course of action in order to optimize action point usage.

[h2][b]CRITICALS[/b][/h2]
When it comes to stat rolls, it is possible to get a critical success now. Luckily for the testers, we have yet to implement critical failures! Obtaining a critical success means that two 6’s have been rolled, and by doing so, the player is presented with optional bonus cards to choose from. 


[h2][b]TRAINING CENTER[/b][/h2]
With the addition of the training center as a location on the map, it gives players an opportunity to try out their skill at any time and prepare themselves for the various puzzles that are associated with cases. This is a simple, and free way to hone those skills, so when you’re faced with a puzzle, you’ll be prepared.
As each puzzle has 3 tiers of difficulty that are directly associated with the case tier difficulty, knowing what you’re potentially up against from the get-go is a safe bet.

[h2][b]SIDE PANEL NOTIFICATIONS[/b][/h2]
With the addition of side panel notification, you’ll always be well informed of what’s going on. Whether it’s an agent requesting your input, or them notifying you that they’ve completed a case, or are heading off, you’ll get a notification on the upper right-hand side of the screen.

[h2][b]REPOSSESSION CASES[/b][/h2]
Although not completely fleshed out, repossession cases are now available in the current build. They are similar in nature to the presently available Security Cases, however, these actually have a few specific puzzles available, namely hotwire and lockpick. 

[h2][b]PUZZLE TWEAKING & BALANCING[/b][/h2]
Even though all of our puzzles are “done” some of them still need some love! We’ve been busy tweaking them and working on the balancing. As we’ve previously mentioned, puzzles have three different tiers of difficulties, so making sure that each tier, of each puzzle, is well balanced is quite the challenge when dealing with 20 puzzles as you can imagine. 

[b]ZERO STATS[/b]
In one of our many recent efforts to begin tackling balancing, we’ve now added “zero stats”. Initially, each agent has a value of 1-5 per for each of the 5 stats, which didn’t give us too much wiggle room in regards to variation.

Also, having certain agents with zero stat values doesn’t necessarily negate their effectiveness, as it is still possible to rely on Action Points or Gear Card usage. As we’ve mentioned before Action Points define the number of actions that an agent can do. 

[h2][b]DEMO PREPERATION[/b][/h2]
We’re busy preparing our demo. This will initially be accessible to the press and influencers and steam curators, but we are planning on making the demo publicly available shortly after. Follow us on social media, or hop on our discord for more details. If you’re a member of the press or an influencer, feel free to get in touch directly.

A lot has changed over the course of the last few weeks, and we here at Gamma Minus would like to show a bit of our progress and the iterations Rough Justice: ‘84 has gone through. Check out the video below to get an overview.

[previewyoutube=oBQIAGwLr7w;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2][b]CONTRACT CHANGES[/b][/h2]
For now, we have settled on having 3 Tier 1, 3 Tier 2, and 3 Tier 3 security contracts when the game starts. This will indubitably change for the demo, but for testing purposes, it’s a great benchmark to assess the overall difficulty of the various tiers. As we went over in our last video, contract tiers indicate the difficulty level of the tier. 1 being easy, 2 being moderate and 3 being hard.

[h2][b]TIER DIFFERENTIATION[/b][/h2]
One of the major changes in regards to contract tiers, especially with this new update, is that Tier 1 contracts auto-repopulate. This gives the player the opportunity to always have something to do, even though it may be low level. 
In order to take on Tier 2 & 3 contracts after the initial batch is completed (or have been removed, for lack of inaction on the player’s part) you’ll have to purchase more. 
This can presently be done in the Agency. You will have to pay, either using money or reputation to unlock batches of contracts. Once you have gained enough reputation you can unlock Night Shift contracts.

[h2][b]DAILY CONTRACTS[/b][/h2]
Don’t want to “pay to play”? No worries, we got you covered. As mentioned, only a certain number of contracts are available at the start of the game, once the Tier 2 and Tier 3 are gone, you’ll have to purchase new ones, and only have Tier 1 contracts available. 
Fresh contracts spawn at 6 am, 9 pm auto spawning stops.

[h2][b]MORAL DECISIONS[/b][/h2]
We’re very excited about this new change! We have started to add moral decision contracts. Initially, they may seem like any other normal contract, in which your agents are required to do either a stat roll or a puzzle, but the player is then presented with a binary choice of how to proceed. These unique contracts have a percentage chance of dropping coveted intel points. 

[h2][b]24/7 CONTRACTS[/b][/h2]
This is a new type of contract that we’ve added since the last update. In total there are 20 24/7 contracts and on any given day 3 of them will be on the map. These contracts can be repeated ad nauseam throughout the day. They are very direct contracts and the goal or rather challenge, be it a puzzle or a stat roll is clearly indicated in the contract title.
The purpose of these contracts is for players to at least be able to do something with their agents and hopefully earn a bit of money. These contracts are not lucrative, but they are a steady constant throughout the day. 

[h2][b]CONTRACT TIER COLORS[/b][/h2]
Each contract tier has an associated color now. This may or may not change, however, we feel as if it is a quality of life mechanic that allows you to easily see the overview of the presently available contract tiers. 

[h2][b]DECISION EQUIPMENT[/b][/h2]
This has been a feature that many people have requested which we have now since implemented. Previously when making a decision you were presented with two options, and you would see which stat would be involved in the decision, however, you were unable to click on the gear that the agent presently had. With this added mechanic, the choice is a lot more obvious. 

[h2][b]REPUTATION LOSS[/b][/h2]
When you fail a contract not only do you lose money but you also lose reputation now, at least for Tier 2 and Tier 3 contracts. The logic behind losing money is the overhead costs ensued by your agent’s inability to successfully complete the contract, requiring the client to get someone else to do it. The loss of reputation is simply an added malus, as failing contracts do not put your agency in good standing. 
[list]

[*] Range of potential minimum/maximum for gain or loss implemented
[/list]

[h2][b]SHOP[/b][/h2]
A few minor changes to the shop as well:

[*] Tier indication of shop item
[/list]

[/list]
[h3][b]CHEAT CODES[/b][/h3]
In order to speed up the testing and bug fixing at this present stage, as well as to work on the balancing, we have implemented cheat codes. Whether or not we accidentally forget to remove them for our initial public build remains to be seen, however having this extra feature has allowed us to make significant progress with testing and balancing so far.

[h3][b]INFORMANTS WIP[/b][/h3]
We are currently working on the implementation of informants. Informants provide the player with daily goals that the player can aim for. These are not required, however, if informant directives are met within the allocated time frame, then the player reaps the rewards provided by the informant. 

This will also eventually be used for story progression. One key feature that we are aiming for is no forced story progression. Story elements - or as they are referred to in-game as “Operations” will be shown in a similar fashion as to standardized directives from informants. The player can choose when to do them.

A lot has changed over the course of the last few months, and we here at Gamma Minus would like to show a bit of our progress and the iterations Rough Justice: ‘84 has gone through. Check out the video below to get an overview.

[previewyoutube=c-IcYcBjdhw;full][/previewyoutube]


[h2][b]AGENT SYSTEM[/b][/h2]
Each agent has five stats, being Strength, Intelligence, Perception, Reflexes & Empathy, and an associated value representing their proficiency with said stat. Additionally, each Agent has a pre-allocated amount of Actions Points. You can read further information on each agent as well by clicking on their bio.


[h2][b]AGENT HIRING SYSTEM[/b][/h2]
Agents are to be considered temporary employees. They are hired for a short duration of time. This is dependent upon their allocated Action Points. 

In the agent hiring panel, you can see the currently available agents. The pool of available agents is refreshed (currently every 3 hours), so if you don’t see an agent that you like, you can wait it out, or alternatively you can spend reputation points in order to force an agent pool refresh.


[h2][b]AGENT TIERING SYSTEM[/b][/h2]
Currently, there are 10 tiers of agents. You can unlock further tiers of agents by spending reputation points. This is not a guarantee that the new tier agents will necessarily be in the roster, they are simply added to the potential pool of agents. 


[h2][b]ACTION POINT SYSTEM[/b][/h2]
Each “action” required a specific amount of action points, which are then deducted from that individual agent’s action point pool. For example, if an agent has 3 action points then they can potentially do three Tier 1 contracts, as Tier 1 contracts cost 1 action point.  
Once the agent’s action points are depleted, they finish their shift and are removed from the agent roster (at the bottom of the screen). They are added back to the pool (with a potential cooldown) and can be hired again at a later date.


[h2][b]CARD USAGE[/b][/h2]
Each agent has three gear card slots. You can purchase gear for each agent at shops. (More on that in a later update!). Although gear cards cost money, they give agents a significant advantage when doing stat rolls during contracts. 

[h2][b]CONTRACT TYPES[/b][/h2]
There are a number of different contract types in Rough Justice: ‘84, including [b]Security[/b], [b]Repossession[/b], [b]Fugitive Recovery[/b], and [b]Night Shift[/b]. Each contract type has different rules and different rewards. 

[h1][b]CONTRACT TIER TYPES[/b][/h1]
All contract types have three different tiers. The tier value of a contract dictates the difficulty level. A Tier 1 contract can be considered an easy contract, Tier 2 moderate, and Tier 3 difficult. 
Finding the right agent to do the job, that has enough Action Points is crucial. 


[h2][b]CONTRACTS[/b][/h2]
It is imperative to carefully read through the intro text for each contract. There are indications as to which stats may be required, or perhaps a vague indication as to whether a puzzle challenge and maybe even as to which one could potentially be in the contract. The wording is sometimes pretty straightforward, whereas other times it may be a bit cryptic, so it’s definitely worth reading the contract description so you know what to expect. Blitzing through the text only to find out that your agent required high strength, but you send an agent with very little strength can end up being a costly mistake.

[h2][b]CHALLENGES[/b][/h2]
There are two challenge types, being stat roll & puzzles. 

[h3][b]DICE ROLL MECHANIC (STATS)[/b][/h3]
As previously mentioned, each Agent has 5 stats and an associated value representing their proficiency with said stat. This value is the determining factor that dictates how many dice the agent is allocated for a stat roll.

In the case of a Tier 1 Security contract, the amount of “successes” is one. The legend below shows what is considered a success. Here for this contract, a 4, 5, or 6 is considered a success. 

[h3][b]PUZZLES[/b][/h3]
There are 15 different types of “puzzles” or mini-games all of which are era and genre-specific. These puzzles are sprinkled throughout the contracts. Some of them are quite easy and are nice pallet cleansers, but bear in mind that puzzles scale according to the tier difficulty of the contract! 

One of the great incentives of choosing a puzzle challenge is that your agent gains an action point.

[h1][b]THE LOWDOWN[/b][/h1]
Our primary focus right now, is to wrap up our prototype, and we are making good progress. Prototypes are fickle creatures, and it is a real challenge for game developers to define what exactly the prototype is, and to follow through with it accordingly. It begs the age-old question "why do something half-heartedly, and obviously flawed when you can do it right from the get-go?" Well, time and money are the most obvious reasons, but wrapping the concept of "quick and dirty" around your head is the real difficulty. We take pride in our work, and attempting something with half-measures somehow seems....wrong. This is compounded by the fact that Rough Justice is ALL ABOUT data. It is a purely data-driven game, dealing with a plethora of variables, and why start tabulating data incorrectly, right? RIGHT?! Ah...the joys of game development and the rabbit hole of prototyping. Good times!
